relations.subject: xdcr:data-type-conversion
relations.evidence: Note that expressions that attempt to compare values whose data types differ from one another must be handled either by _data-type conversion_ or by _collation comparison_. These procedures, which are performed implicitly, are described in [ XDCR Data-Type Conversion](xdcr-filtering-data-type-conversion.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page names three roles able to configure XDCR filtering - 'Full, Cluster, and XDCR Administrators' - but only 'Full Administrator' resolves to an existing registry concept (role:full-administrator). 'Cluster Administrator' and 'XDCR Administrator' are not elaborated anywhere on this page (no privilege list, no link to learn/security/roles.md, no internal role identifier such as cluster_admin), and roles.md itself is outside this batch's scope. Deliberately left unminted rather than guessed at - a role catalogue should be built from roles.md directly, not inferred from a passing mention on a filtering-reference page.

cross_component_finding: NAMING INCONSISTENCY FOR THE SAME ENUM, WITHIN SERVER'S OWN DOCS. This page states: 'Filtering ... can be used with either the _revision-based_ or the _timestamp-based_ conflict resolution policy.' xdcr-advanced-settings.md (same module, same batch) states: 'The default conflict resolution setting is based on _sequence number_. Alternatively, conflict resolution based on _timestamp_ can be selected.' Both are describing the exact same per-bucket, fixed-at-creation choice that the extraction-layer concept xdcr:conflict-resolution-method already models with values 'Sequence Number | Timestamp' (minted from cloud/clusters/xdcr/xdcr.json, which itself uses 'sequence number' and 'timestamp'). So within this one module, the same enum member is called 'revision-based' on one page and 'sequence number' on another (with 'timestamp'/'timestamp-based' the shared second value) - a same-mechanism-different-name split of exactly the kind round 19 warned about, found here between two sibling pages in the SAME batch rather than across products.
cross_product_finding: Capella's manage-xdcr-replications.md (round 7) states a Server-version gate on a 'Filter Binary Documents' checkbox: 'If your operational cluster is on Couchbase Server version 7.2.2 or later, choose whether to **Filter Binary Documents**.' None of this batch's five Server-side filtering reference pages (this one, xdcr-filtering-expressions.md, xdcr-regular-expressions.md, xdcr-filtering-data-type-conversion.md, or the module intro) mention 'binary' documents, a binary data type gate, or the 7.2.2 version threshold at all - the word 'Binary' appears only once in the whole batch, as a data-type name (highest-magnitude entry in xdcr-filtering-data-type-conversion.md's precedence table), an unrelated sense. This is a one-way documentation asymmetry: Capella's UI-guide names a specific filtering capability and its version gate that the underlying Server reference manual, read directly, never restates.
